meta.title: {{name}} — transitions for Minecraft video creators
meta.description: Pick a template, tweak it, preview in real time, and export transition clips with an alpha channel. A free, open-source desktop app.

hero.lead: {{name}} is a desktop app: pick a template, tweak a few parameters, preview in real time, and export a short clip with an alpha channel to drop over the cut in your editor.
hero.facts: Free & open source · Windows · Fully offline
hero.viewerNote: Rendered live in your browser by the app’s own engine.
hero.demoAssets: The web version uses flat demo colors; the desktop app reads your installed game and resource packs.
hero.noWebgl: This browser doesn’t support WebGL2, so the live preview can’t run.
hero.mcAssets: Block and item textures on this page come from Minecraft {{version}}, © Mojang / Microsoft, and are shown here for demonstration only. The desktop app reads your installed game and resource packs; no game files ship with it.

sim.title: Try it before you install.
sim.lead: The window below is the desktop editor itself: the same interface code, the same render engine, the same built-in templates. Pick a template, drag parameters, scrub the timeline, press Space to play — all of it runs in your browser.
sim.autoStart: It starts on its own when you scroll here, or you can start it now.
sim.exportNote: There’s no FFmpeg in the browser: exporting really renders every frame, but no file is written.
sim.compactTitle: Your screen is a little narrow
sim.compact: The full editor needs a wider screen. Here you can preview and switch templates; open this page on a computer for the whole thing.

desktopOnly.packs: Adding resource packs needs the desktop app.
desktopOnly.vanilla: Reading your Minecraft install needs the desktop app.
desktopOnly.templates: Installing, exporting and saving templates needs the desktop app.

desktopOnly.folder: Choosing an output folder needs the desktop app.

sim.desktopOnlyHint: This step reads or writes files on your computer, which a web page can’t do.
sim.exportDone: Every one of those frames went through the real export pipeline. In the desktop app, FFmpeg writes them to “{{format}}”, ready to drop into your editor.

templates.title: {{count}} built-in templates, all rendered live.
templates.lead: Each card plays frames the render engine just drew in your browser — not screenshots, not videos. Built-in templates load through the same path as the ones you write yourself.

alpha.title: Exports with an alpha channel
alpha.body: Lay it on a track above your footage — no keying needed. Four formats:

frames.title: The preview is the render
frames.body: Every frame is a pure function of time. Preview and export run the same rendering code, so each exported frame matches what you saw — with optional subframe motion blur.

stack.title: Bring your own assets
stack.body: A three-layer resource stack: built-in, your game’s vanilla assets, your resource packs — upper layers win. Add a pack and the transition reskins itself. Game files are read locally and never copied or uploaded.

offline.title: Fully offline
offline.body: No accounts, telemetry, auto-updates or crash reporting. Template scripts run in an isolated worker with no network, files or UI.

extend.title: Extensible templates
extend.body: Presets, derived templates, template package import and export, and script templates written in TypeScript. The properties panel is generated from each template’s manifest.

bilingual.title: Chinese and English, dark and light
bilingual.body: Two languages and two themes that follow your system — or switch them yourself.

workflow.title: Three steps, from launch to export.
workflow.lead: The design goal: under 30 seconds from opening the app to exporting your first transition, with no manual to read.

pick.title: Pick a template
pick.body: Transitions or overlays. Covers in the library come alive when you hover them.

tune.title: Tweak it
tune.body: Blocks, order, timing, easing… every change shows up in the preview on the next frame, and one undo takes it back.

export.title: Export
export.body: Choose a format, resolution and frame rate, drop the clip into your editor and line up the cut point.

open.title: Open, free, and built together.
open.lead: The source code is public on GitHub under the GPL-3.0 license. Issues, templates and pull requests are all welcome.
